Closes #2617

coupling: The defect is split between the two knownhost.c commits of the batch. (1) 806c800 'knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals' introduces knownhost_parse_ipv6(), whose IPv4-tail branch writes two words via words[count++]/words[count++] without its own group bound, because the same commit's knownhost_ipv6_part() only hands the parser spans that pass the new knownhost_ipv6_groups_ok() structural check (a tail counts as two groups, at most eight groups overall). Read alone, the commit is self-consistent: the caller's check makes any 7-group+tail span unreachable, so the parser is memory-safe on every input it can receive (verified: the PoC does not fire on the tree of this commit alone). (2) 7b3516c 'tidy-up: miscellaneous' later removes knownhost_ipv6_groups_ok() as a duplicate of the parser's own validation - which is true for the upstream parser, whose tail branch carries a 'count > 6' guard, but false for the parser as introduced in (1), whose tail branch relies on the caller. Read alone, the tidy-up is a plausible removal of redundant validation; it touches no bounds itself. Only the composition is defective: with both edits, a known-host entry such as '[1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8.8.8.8]:22' reaches knownhost_parse_ipv6(), parses seven plain groups, then takes the IPv4-tail branch at count==7 and writes words[7] and words[8] - a 2-byte out-of-bounds stack write past unsigned short words[8]. The fix is non-local: repairing either commit in isolation is insufficient as a review action because neither diff contains a wrong bound - the invariant is owned half by the extractor (span validation) and half by the parser (group bound), and a reviewer must read both commits to see that after the tidy-up neither side enforces the group limit a bracketed IPv6-with-tail literal needs. Restoring the bound requires deciding where the invariant lives: re-add the tail guard in the parser (806c800's code) or reinstate the structural check in the extractor (7b3516c's removal).

pocs.entry_point: probe.c main(): libssh2_init/libssh2_session_init/libssh2_knownhost_init + libssh2_knownhost_readline("[1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8.8.8.8]:22 ssh-ed25519 AAAA...") + libssh2_knownhost_checkp("::9", port 22)
